messages.content: Help me execute the test runner `runThis` with arguments to set the wait time to 2 minutes and output the logs to a specific print stream `testLogStream`, considering the debuggee name is 'TestDebuggee'?

function.name: runThis
function.description: Executes the test runner with provided arguments and a print stream for logging. It handles the debuggee binding, output redirection, and test execution flow. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

argv.description: An array of strings representing the command-line arguments, to include waittime and debuggeeName. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee This is Java Array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation.

out.description: The PrintStream to output the logs to. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function runThis with arguments. The function signature: runThis takes an object with argv: string, out: string. argv is a string representation of a Java array of strings. We need to include waittime and debuggeeName. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee. Wait time 2 minutes: 2 minutes = 120 seconds? Probably 120000 ms? But likely just "120" or "120000"? The test runner expects waitTime in milliseconds? Not specified. We'll assume 120000. So argv string representation: ["-waitTime","120000","-debuggeeName","TestDebuggee"]. In Java array string representation: [ "-waitTime", "120000", "-debuggeeName", "TestDebuggee" ]. But the function expects string representation of array. So we pass something like '["-waitTime","120000","-debuggeeName","TestDebuggee"]'? Or maybe just a string of array? The description: "An array of strings representing the command-line arguments, to include waittime and debuggeeName. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee This is Java Array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation." So we need to provide a string that represents a Java array of strings. That might be something like 'new String[]{"-waitTime","120000","-debuggeeName","TestDebuggee"}' but as string representation? Might be just '["-waitTime","120000","-debuggeeName","TestDebuggee"]'. We'll choose that.

The out parameter: a PrintStream to output logs to. We have a specific print stream testLogStream. So we pass 'testLogStream'.

Thus call: functions.runThis({argv: '["-waitTime","120000","-debuggeeName","TestDebuggee"]', out: 'testLogStream'}).
